records.text: White now has a passed pawn: no enemy pawn ahead on the same or adjacent files. That does not establish promotion.
Black now has a passed pawn: no enemy pawn ahead on the same or adjacent files. That does not establish promotion.
The better move would create a passed pawn for White, with no enemy pawn ahead on its own or adjacent files.
The better move would create a passed pawn for Black, with no enemy pawn ahead on its own or adjacent files.

The better move would leave Black with an isolated pawn, lacking friendly pawns on the adjacent files.

Under the better alternative, Black would have doubled pawns sharing a file.

The knight develops with its first move from its original square.
This is the knight's first departure from its starting square. Development has begun.
A previously unmoved knight has come off its home square.
The change here is knight development: its first move away from its starting position.
The bishop develops for the first time, leaving its starting square.
This bishop had not moved before. It now leaves its original square.
Bishop development begins here, with a first departure from home.
A bishop comes off its initial square. It is its first move, not a redeployment.
The better move would develop a knight for the first time, off its original square.
Another choice would begin the knight's development with its first departure from home.
The alternative would move a previously unmoved knight away from its starting square.
The better choice includes first-time knight development. It would bring that knight off its original square.

This move leaves a weaker position than the best available choice. The comparison establishes the cost.
